questions: Did the shaking begin suddenly or over a period of hours to days?
Can the shaking stop when you deliberately relax the hand or become distracted?
Does the shaking change noticeably in speed or severity from moment to moment?
Does it lessen when you voluntarily copy the same movement with the other hand?
Does the shaking occur when the hand is completely at rest?
Does it mainly occur when you hold the hand out or use it?
Do you have weakness in the affected arm or hand?
Do you have numbness or altered sensation in that arm or hand?
Do you have difficulty speaking, seeing, walking, or maintaining your balance?
Have you had a recent head, neck, or limb injury?
Have you recently started, stopped, or changed the dose of any medication?
Do you use stimulant drugs, excess caffeine, or thyroid medication?
Have you had similar shaking elsewhere in your body?
Does anyone in your family have a tremor or Parkinson’s disease?
Have you been under unusual stress or emotional strain recently?

results: 1. distractibility testing (complex motor task with the unaffected side): POSITIVE - the tremor decreases or stops when the left arm performs a task such as drinking from a cup
2. entrainment testing (tap to an externally paced rhythm): POSITIVE - amplitude falls and the rhythm becomes irregular under repetitive voluntary movement of the other side
3. co-activation sign on passive movement of the affected limb: POSITIVE - movement of the contralateral arm co-activates the hand with an increase in tremor intensity
4. 'whack-a-mole' sign (restrain the affected limb and watch the others): POSITIVE - passive fixation of the hand increases movement in the arm and shoulder
5. variability of amplitude, frequency and axis over the examination: irregular, variable frequency around 4-6 Hz, at times combined with myoclonic jerks
6. video-EEG monitoring with limb surface electrodes: 24 h recording with right-arm surface electrodes: irregular tremor, relatively high frequency with irregularities, no epileptiform correlate

DIAGNOSIS: Functional tremor as a functional neurological movement disorder (nonepileptic, nonstructural tremor with functional motor-network dysfunction)
